diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive loss on this customer's fibre path. RX power declined from the normal range near -19.17 dBm to the degraded range near -26.45 dBm, with a current live reading of -27.1 dBm. TX power, TX bias, and distance remain stable, ruling out laser ageing and a path-geometry change. The elevated re-authentication rate and short sessions are symptoms of the degrading optical link.
evidence: The customer's RX power started at approximately -19.17 dBm, which is normal, and declined steadily to approximately -26.45 dBm, which is degraded.
The live ONU probe confirms the condition with RX at -27.1 dBm; the ONU is still online and responding.
TX power remains around +2.3 dBm and TX bias remains stable near 11 mA, so there is no evidence of laser degradation.
Distance is constant at 188, so there is no fibre-path geometry or record-assignment step change.
Peers on EPON0/3 have healthy optical levels, so the fault is isolated to this customer's path rather than the PON port, splitter, or OLT.
The one other offline ONU on the port is a single definite negative among healthy peers and is consistent with an independent ONU outage; it does not establish a shared failure.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, and temperature, and all tested PONs are healthy.

The customer has 9 sessions in 24 hours with a 71-minute average duration, indicating flapping, but the defined decision rule attributes this to the optical decline because the link trend began in the normal band and ended degraded.
RADIUS credentials and line ID are consistent, VLAN 1013 is correctly provisioned, and the router heartbeat is healthy, ruling out authentication, VLAN, router, and provisioning faults.
PON traffic levels do not demonstrate congestion; the customer's progressive optical decline is the primary fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre maintenance for EPON0/3:14. Inspect and clean the ONU, ODF, splitter, connectors, and customer drop; perform optical-loss and OTDR testing; repair or replace the degraded connector, splice, drop, or fibre section. Recheck RX power, session stability, and traffic after repair. Do not replace the OLT or PON splitter based on this evidence.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
